verdicts.reason: Both require a concrete implementable alternative plus an explanation of how it still serves the proposal's stated objective, with identical zero anchors.
Identical list of monitoring elements (indicators, data collection, verification, reporting, revisit triggers) with the same zero anchor, only reordered prose.
Both score whether a concrete, implementation-ready alternative design is offered; 'specific enough to write into the rule' is a sharper phrasing of 'concrete enough to be implemented'.
Word-for-word equivalent test of whether the whole argument rests on first-person anecdote with no external sourcing.
Same enumerated workflow markers (forms, offices, transition steps, testing scenarios, timelines, documentation) and same 'general preference only' floor.
Both score a claimed multi-party/consensus self-presentation with named parties versus a clearly individual submission; the added no-verification note does not change the target.
Both score disclosure of prior permits, recurring meetings, ongoing communications, or past dealings with the agency, presence only.
Both score a reasoned failure mechanism explaining why the rule would not produce the agency's intended effect, judging reasoning rather than tone.
Both score whether new record information (measurements, operational records, surveys, field observations) with a stated source enters the record.
Both require the commenter's own quantified compliance-cost estimate with its basis stated; 'dollar figures' and 'numeric cost estimate' pick out the same submissions in practice.
Both score accurate connection of the proposal to statutory language, delegated authority, precedent, or legal limits versus unsupported legal assertion.
Both require concrete firsthand observation translated into a generalizable rule-relevant pattern, with bare anecdote or emotion at zero.
Both score identification of specific populations/firms/places bearing distinct costs and benefits plus an account of unequal exposure.
Both score surface duplication of wording, headings, demands, or paragraph order from a form/campaign submission versus individualized wording.
Same enumerated wrapper artifacts (portal/email headers, attachment placeholders, filenames, OCR errors, duplicated cover text) scored as surface residue.
Both require naming an exact proposed provision and stating a concrete revision, with bare support/opposition at zero.
Both score prominence of advertised organizational size, market share, longevity, assets, employees, facilities, or senior titles.
Both score only the letter furniture (formal salutation plus signature block); the explicit intermediate anchor merely spells out the implied scale.
Both score precise mapping of the proposal onto docket provisions, CFR sections, statutory authority, or requested edits.
Both score supply of exact replacement language, thresholds, definitions, procedures, or parameters versus 'do more'/'act quickly'/bare position.
Both score attention to responsible actors, workflows, training, system dependencies, and failure modes versus treating implementation as automatic.
X scores the surface presence of part/section CFR citations while Y scores a developed ultra-vires legal argument; a comment can easily have one without the other.
Identical three-anchor gap-identification rubric; only prose versus '10 =' formatting differs.
Both are the same purely surface test for any digit-bearing quantity anywhere in the text, use-agnostic.
X measures emotional intensity of the register while Y measures reported first-hand operational practice; a calm practitioner or an outraged non-participant separates them.
Same procedural-request rubric with the same 10/5/0 anchors and the same enumerated procedural actions and reason requirement.
Same ambiguity rubric requiring a quoted/cited term, two readings, and divergent consequences, with identical 5 and 0 anchors.
Both score discrimination of strong from weak evidence, naming of assumptions or limitations, and confidence calibrated to support.
Both score an explicit step-by-step causal chain including behavioral response versus bare assertion of harm or benefit; the added partial-credit note does not shift the property.
